\begin{tikzpicture}[font=\small, >=Stealth]
  \draw[->, line width=0.9pt] (-3.2,0)--(-0.2,0); \draw[->, line width=0.9pt] (3.2,0)--(0.2,0);
  \node[above] at (-2.0,0.05) {$e^-$: $p = (E, E\hat{\mathbf z})$};
  \node[below] at (2.0,-0.05) {$e^+$: $p' = (E, -E\hat{\mathbf z})$};
  \draw[->, line width=0.9pt, figB] (0,0)--(1.9,1.55); \draw[->, line width=0.9pt, figB] (0,0)--(-1.9,-1.55);
  \node[figB, right] at (1.9,1.62) {$\mu^-$: $k = (E, \mathbf k)$};
  \node[figB, left] at (-1.9,-1.62) {$\mu^+$: $k' = (E, -\mathbf k)$};
  \draw[gray] (0.95,0) arc (0:39.2:0.95); \node at (1.22,0.36) {$\theta$};
  \draw[->, gray] (3.6,0)--(4.3,0); \node[font=\scriptsize, gray, right] at (4.3,0) {$\hat{\mathbf z}$};
  \node[align=left, anchor=west, font=\footnotesize] at (5.3,0.2) {$E = \tfrac12E_{\rm cm}$ for all four particles\\[2pt] $|\mathbf p| = E$ \ ($m_e = 0$)\\[2pt] $|\mathbf k| = \sqrt{E^2 - m_\mu^2}$\\[2pt] $\mathbf k\cdot\hat{\mathbf z} = |\mathbf k|\cos\theta$};
